selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Fix Our Forests Act establishes new requirements and programs for managing federal, state, tribal, and private lands to reduce wildfire risks, expedite environmental reviews, and improve forest health. It creates an interagency Fireshed Center to predict and assess fires, establishes emergency management projects in high-risk firesheds, reforms litigation procedures for forest management projects, creates community wildfire risk reduction and research programs, expands utilities' ability to manage vegetation near power lines, and provides casualty assistance for wildland firefighters.

affected_groups.effect: The U.S. Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management must designate fireshed areas, conduct assessments, carry out emergency management projects, and update reporting and tracking procedures.

Receive assistance through a new Wildland Fire Management Casualty Assistance Program providing support, travel expense reimbursements, and case management for line-of-duty injuries, illnesses, or deaths.
Gain expanded permissions to clear trees and vegetation up to 150 feet from power lines on public lands and benefit from streamlined review processes and categorical exclusions for maintenance plans.

Can enter into shared stewardship agreements, participate in fireshed assessments, utilize good neighbor authorities, and apply for consolidated wildfire mitigation grants through a new interagency portal.

key_provisions: Designates high-risk fireshed management areas and establishes a joint U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Geological Survey Fireshed Center along with a public Fireshed Registry.

Expedites environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and expands existing categorical exclusions to cover up to 10,000 acres for fireshed management and hazardous fuels reduction projects.

Implements litigation reforms that limit courts' ability to issue injunctions, restrict available remedies to agency remands, and impose strict deadlines and standing requirements for legal challenges.
Establishes a Community Wildfire Risk Reduction Program and a Community Wildfire Defense Research Program to support building codes, home hardening, and an application portal for grants.
Permits electric utilities to conduct vegetation management and remove hazard trees up to 150 feet from power lines on rights-of-way, and grants categorical exclusions for these utility activities.

Creates biochar demonstration and research grant projects, a white oak restoration initiative across multiple federal and non-federal programs, and a Wildland Fire Management Casualty Assistance Program for firefighters and their families.
missing_information: Specific funding levels, appropriations amounts, or exact fiscal costs required to implement the various new centers, grant programs, and research initiatives.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Fix Our Forests Act establishes new requirements and programs for managing federal, state, tribal, and private lands to reduce wildfire risks, expedite environmental reviews, and improve forest health. It creates an interagency Fireshed Center to predict and assess fires, establishes emergency management projects in high-risk firesheds, reforms litigation procedures for forest management projects, creates community wildfire risk reduction and research programs, expands utilities' ability to manage vegetation near power lines, and provides casualty assistance for wildland firefighters.
summary_detail.significance: The bill enacts sweeping changes to federal forest management, environmental review timelines, and judicial oversight for public lands. By prioritizing emergency wildfire risk reduction through expedited reviews and restricted litigation, it substantially alters how federal agencies and partners address overgrown forests, potentially affecting millions of acres of federal and adjacent lands.
